prompt: Why do hardening guides tell you to reference third-party actions by full commit SHA rather than tag?
explanation: A tag or branch is a pointer someone can move, so `@v3` today is not a promise about tomorrow; a full commit SHA names exactly one immutable tree. Pinning is how you make a third-party dependency in your pipeline reviewable and stable.

options.text: SHAs resolve faster on the runner
Tags are mutable — they can be re-pointed at different code; a SHA cannot
